images.year_evidence: CARVED — the date 1887 is cut into the escutcheon on the facade, reported by the operator from the building itself. Corroborating documents: permit filed 13 February 1886 (Bulletin municipal officiel, 14 Feb 1886); PSS estimates completion c.1888. The carved date sits between the two and outranks the estimate.
images.street: 31 rue de la Chaussée d'Antin / 71 rue de Provence (current tenant: Onyx)
images.shows: A dated POST-1884 commercial corner. Built three years after the Alphand decree of 23 July 1884, so designed under the arc-comble regime rather than the 45° one, yet reads as a classic haussmannien corner to most eyes. The strongest available argument for date-window chronology over a period enum, and the only dated anchor outside Daly's 1864 window. Also the pan coupé case.
images.quality_note: 340x255 thumbnail — enough to establish massing and corner form, too small to judge the roofline or read the escutcheon.
images.open_question: Is the comble the post-1884 arc or a straight 45°? Not resolvable at this resolution.
